A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FoMo-0D. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including the landscape result tables and extensively relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original FoMo-0D results on 57 ADBench datasets, ablations, runtime measurements and an attention case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original OpenOOD-derived evaluations, GMM goodness-of-fit results and expanded attention analysis.

M1.justification: The GMM data prior, cross-entropy training, router attention, dataset reuse, linear transformations and single-pass inference remain unchanged. The additional evaluations reuse the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix H.2 adds ten image-derived OD datasets: ImageNet200 and ImageNet1K each paired with SSB-hard, NINCO, iNaturalist, Textures and OpenImage-O. These extend evaluation to novel-class OOD scenarios represented through image embeddings; all 57 original ADBench datasets remain.

E2.justification: The original 26 baselines and four hyperparameter-averaged variants remain. The new OpenOOD comparisons reuse DTE-NP, kNN, ICL and DTE-C, all already evaluated in v1; no new detection comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets, ADBench splits and metrics remain unchanged. Added evaluations specify OpenOOD datasets with 10,000 samples, 5% outliers and 512-dimensional ResNet18 features, alongside fitted-GMM comparisons and a high-likelihood-inlier control for the attention study.

E4.justification: Appendix H.1 adds a substantial investigation linking GMM goodness of fit to performance across all 57 datasets. Appendix G extends v1's attention study with a high-likelihood-inlier comparison and three individual-outlier visualizations. Existing ablations are retained and relocated to Appendix F.

E5.justification: v2 adds an energy two-sample goodness-of-fit test in H.1 and another one-sided Wilcoxon comparison in Appendix G. The existing five-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting and main benchmark significance-testing practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 8–10 add OpenOOD and combined 67-dataset results. FoMo-0D averages 53.40 and 52.10 AUROC on the ImageNet200- and ImageNet1K-derived sets, respectively, below ICL and DTE-C's means. New prior-fit findings and an attention-control p-value of 0.99 are also reported. Original benchmark table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Mahalanobis and chi-squared properties, and linear-transform preservation proofs are retained from v1 Appendix A in v2 Appendix C. Renumbering and cross-reference corrections do not change their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: v2's abstract adds an 'at least 7x speed-up compared to previous methods' claim, strengthening v1's runtime statement despite retaining the 7.7 ms measurement. The central novelty, zero-shot model-selection and ADBench performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds interpretations distinguishing successful and unsuccessful transfer beyond fitted GMMs, and hypothesizes why non-parametric baselines struggle on high-dimensional OpenOOD features. Appendix G extends the attention interpretation to combining boundary and neighbor information. Existing limitations remain in Appendix M.

D1.justification: The new analyses identify the energy package's e-test and specify ResNet18 average-pooling feature extraction for OpenOOD. Existing architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware and the code/checkpoint access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for ResNet, goodness-of-fit testing, LLaMA and OpenOOD. The substantive positioning against previous PFNs and OD research remains largely unchanged, with related discussion relocated to Appendices K–L.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively condensed and rewritten. Detailed setup, ablations, related work and discussion are reorganized into appendices, with a new appendix contents guide and a shorter main conclusion.

P2.justification: v2 adds the individual-outlier attention and GMM-fit plots in Figures 15–16 and OpenOOD Tables 8–10. Numerous retained figures and tables are relocated or resized, including moving ablation displays into Appendix F and scaling down several landscape result tables.

improvement.justification: The new prior-fit analysis, OpenOOD evaluation and attention controls make generalization more assessable, while the restructuring improves navigation. These provide a limited net benefit. However, the new blanket 7x speedup is not established by unchanged Table 3, and the second-or-third-place OpenOOD description conflicts with fourth-place Textures results in Tables 8–9.
